original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Measure and verify bounded, source-bound process-local reuse of exact child-cost intervals in the unchanged selected-word seven-lever planner, preserving every model check, bisection and complete typed rational trace.
scope_change_reason: The first drawn runtime card is narrowed to the selected-word cost planner. Profiling identified exact exponential bounds as its bottleneck. This is distinct from PR2414 native compilation reuse and is not a claim about full selected cold replay.
bottleneck_link: Repeated exact cost screens are used to reject or budget mechanism candidates. Reusing pure intervals under unchanged dependencies reduces those screens while retaining model constraints and exact source arithmetic.
stop_rule: Measure unchanged uncached/fill/warm fixtures with full trace equality, test argument/dependency invalidation and publish only the scoped measured result. Stop without a speed claim if evidence differs.
evidence: Source-pinned original engine and seven-lever script; exact1771-event trace; 1238 child requests,263 model checks,263 relaxation sums and7 ceilings;12 controls; five entry-point groups; before/fill/warm benchmark with complete comparisons.
author: Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in implementation, verification, profiling and writing. No subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: How much reuse occurs in a real sequence of different candidate profiles?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The measured warm repetitions do not establish end-to-end throughput on a candidate search.
open_questions.first_step: Pin one candidate sequence and compare complete traces, miss rates, bounded evictions and first-fill cost.
open_questions.blocked_by: No production candidate stream is supplied by this seven-lever fixture.

open_questions.question: Should the opt-in session be integrated into a production planner?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A caller needs a reviewed serial API, dependency boundary and memory budget.
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate one concrete caller against the source guard and full-trace comparison.
open_questions.blocked_by: Production integration and broader replay performance are outside this package.

selection.method: Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.

upstream_checkpoint.retry_note: The first Discussion refresh hit a transient HTTP/2 REFUSED_STREAM; the recorded retry completed with fresh full pagination.
upstream_checkpoint.decision: Continue the scoped pure interval cache; only our own claim matched this planner mechanism. PR2414 compilation reuse remains distinct.
